books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

primary_sources: Rutherford B. Hayes, Inaugural Address, March 5, 1877

stimulus.text:
“The evils which afflict the Southern States can only be removed or remedied by the united and harmonious efforts of both races, actuated by motives of mutual sympathy and regard; and while in duty bound and fully determined to protect the rights of all by every constitutional means at the disposal of my Administration, I am sincerely anxious to use every legitimate influence in favor of honest and efficient local self-government as the true resource of those States for the promotion of the contentment and prosperity of their citizens.”

—President Rutherford B. Hayes, Inaugural Address, March 5, 1877
stimulus.source_note: Rutherford B. Hayes, Inaugural Address, March 5, 1877. Public domain (presidential address; text verified against the Miller Center transcript and Wikisource).

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: In this passage, Hayes’s call for “honest and efficient local self-government” most directly signaled that he would

options.text: withdraw federal troops and let Southern states govern themselves.
send more federal troops to protect Black voters.
options.misconception: “Local self-government” points the other way, toward removing federal power, not adding it.

options.text: ask Congress to pass a new Reconstruction Act.
options.misconception: Background: Hayes asked for no new Reconstruction law; his program was reconciliation.

options.text: refuse to take office until the disputed election was settled in court.
options.misconception: Background: Hayes took office in March 1877 after the Electoral Commission’s decision.

rationales.A: “Local self-government” was Hayes’s polite way of saying the federal occupation was over. Within weeks, the last troops left South Carolina and Louisiana, and Southern Democrats took charge.
rationales.B: “Local self-government” points the other way, toward removing federal power, not adding it.
rationales.C: Background: Hayes asked for no new Reconstruction law; his program was reconciliation.
rationales.D: Background: Hayes took office in March 1877 after the Electoral Commission’s decision.
rationales.general:
1. Hayes calls local self-government the South’s “true resource,” the thing that will bring contentment.
2. Local self-government means government by Southerners, not by federal soldiers and officials.
3. Background: within weeks of this address, Hayes ordered the last troops out of South Carolina and Louisiana.
4. The phrase was the public announcement of the bargain struck to settle the election.
Remember: presidents often announce a hard decision in gentle words, so listen for what the gentle words actually do.
